extracted.intended_audience: students and practitioners learning Tufte-style minimalist data visualization in R (ggplot2/ggthemes/ggExtra)
extracted.subtask_description: Apply Edward Tufte's data-ink principles to produce minimalist, high data-ink-ratio graphics (line plots, scatterplots, boxplots, bar charts, sparklines) using R and ggplot2-related packages. Includes concrete techniques (range-frames, rugs, marginal plots, geom_tufteboxplot, sparklines) and implementation notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data-ink (definition and data-ink ratio)
rubrics_metrics.description: The term 'data-ink' is defined as the total ink on a graph that represents data. The data-ink ratio is the proportion of a graphic’s ink devoted to the non-redundant display of data-information; it should equal (1 - the proportion of graphics that can be erased without loss of data-information).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maximize the portion of ink that encodes data; consider what parts of a graphic could be erased without losing data-information. Use this quantitative notion to judge additions (axes, gridlines, boxes, heavy styling) as potentially non-data-ink.

rubrics_metrics.name: Above all else show data
rubrics_metrics.description: Tufte's primary principle: 'Above all else show data.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make the data the dominant visual element. Avoid decorations and non-informative elements that draw attention away from the data itself.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximize the data-ink ratio
rubrics_metrics.description: Design graphics so that the proportion of ink devoted to non-redundant data-information is as large as possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer minimal themes and remove visual elements that do not add new information. When adding elements, ensure they directly support data interpretation rather than ornamentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Erase non-data-ink
rubrics_metrics.description: Remove ink in a graphic that does not represent data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eliminate decorative gridlines, heavy axis boxes, backgrounds, shading, and other elements that serve only aesthetic purposes. Use theme settings (e.g., theme_tufte) to reduce non-data ink.

rubrics_metrics.name: Erase redundant data-ink
rubrics_metrics.description: Remove redundant representations of the same data-information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid repeating the same information in multiple visual forms unless each repetition adds clarity. For example, don't label every tick if the labels are unnecessary, and avoid duplicative legends when direct annotation is possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revise and edit data-ink (iterative editing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Continuously revise and edit graphics to remove unnecessary ink and clarify the data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat graphics as drafts: iteratively remove elements and simplify until only necessary ink remains. Use small edits (removing axes, ticks, boxes, or redundant labels) and compare whether the data-information is preserved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimal line plot
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep the data-ink ratio high by removing extra lines/points and non-essential axes; minimal line plots omit axis decorations and focus on the line/points representing the data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example guidance: use geom_line() + geom_point(size=small) with theme_tufte(), remove axis titles (axis.title=element_blank()), format axis labels compactly (e.g., scale_y_continuous with formatted labels), and annotate the series label directly on the plot rather than using heavy axes or legends.

rubrics_metrics.name: Range-frame (quartile-frame) scatterplot
rubrics_metrics.description: Use axis lines only on the range of the data points (range-frame) rather than full traditional axes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide only the most appropriate axis lines for the data range (e.g., with geom_rangeframe()). This reduces non-data-ink while still giving scale context; adjust axis titles/positions as needed for clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dot-dash (rug) scatterplot
rubrics_metrics.description: Augment scatterplots with tick marks (rugs) next to axes to represent marginal distributions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use geom_rug() to show marginal distributions without adding heavy marginal plots. Turning off ticks in the theme (ticks=F) can further reduce non-data-ink while preserving marginal information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Marginal histogram (and density/boxplot) scatterplot
rubrics_metrics.description: Show marginal distributions using small histograms (or density/boxplot alternatives) to convey distributional structure, especially for large data sets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use ggMarginal() with type='histogram' for large point clouds; alternatives type='density' or type='boxplot' are provided depending on the message. Prefer marginal displays when raw point overlap obscures distributional shape.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimal boxplot
rubrics_metrics.description: Design boxplots to use as little non-data ink as possible (e.g., remove the box and use a dot and blank space to represent median and IQR).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use geom_tufteboxplot() to implement minimal boxplots; make outlier points transparent if they add clutter (outlier.colour='transparent'); hide axis titles if annotation near the plot suffices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimal barchart
rubrics_metrics.description: Create bar charts without grid or axes lines, using minimal visual cues; add subtle Tufte-like ablines for reference if needed, and tune bar width/spacing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply theme_tufte(base_size, ticks=F), set geom_bar(width=small, fill='gray', stat='identity'), remove axis titles, use scale_y_continuous with sensible breaks, and draw subtle horizontal lines (geom_hline) to provide gentle reference lines rather than heavy grids.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sparklines (word-sized graphics)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use small, intense, word-sized graphics that can be embedded inline with text or tables—sparklines should be simple and typographically precise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sparklines must be small and single; when grouping multiple sparklines, ensure consistent scaling across them. Show only essential points (e.g., min/max/last), use very small line sizes, facet with free_y when appropriate, and annotate critical values near the lines rather than adding axes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annotate near data rather than rely on heavy axes/legends
rubrics_metrics.description: Where appropriate, label series or values directly on the plot instead of using verbose axes or external legends to reduce non-data-ink.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use annotate('text', ...) or geom_text with nudges to place labels close to data endpoints or important points (e.g., end-of-series labels for sparklines). This preserves scale context while eliminating the need for heavy axis elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose marginal display type based on data density
rubrics_metrics.description: Select marginal histogram, density, or boxplot based on the amount and nature of data: histograms for huge point clouds; density or boxplot alternatives as appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When many points cause overplotting, use histogram marginals; when distributional smoothness is desired, choose density; when summarizing spread succinctly, use marginal boxplots. The chosen marginal should add information with minimal extra ink.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use minimal-themed tools and functions (implementation guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Leverage available R packages and functions that implement Tufte-style minimalism (ggplot2, ggthemes/geom_rangeframe/geom_tufteboxplot, ggExtra::ggMarginal, geom_rug, theme_tufte, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply theme_tufte() and the listed geometries to implement the described minimal plots. The chapter provides concrete code examples for each plot type; use these as starting templates and then iteratively remove non-essential elements to maximize data-ink.
